Air at Mach number M1 = 2.0 enters a frictionless, isentropic, quasi-1D converging nozzle with area ratio A2/A1 = 0.7.
Use the specific heat ratio γ = 1.4 for air.
Use the gas constant R = 287 J/(kg·K) for air.
Solve for the exit Mach number M2 on the supersonic branch of the isentropic area-to-Mach relation A/A* = (1/M)·[(2/(γ+1))·(1 + (γ−1)/2·M²)]^((γ+1)/(2(γ−1))), using A2/A* = 0.7·(A1/A*) where A1/A* is evaluated at M1 = 2.0.
The resulting M2 will be less than 2.0, reflecting deceleration from area decrease in supersonic flow.
Assume a stagnation temperature T0 = 288 K (standard sea-level value) and state this assumption explicitly in the solution, since T0 is not given in the problem.
Compute the inlet static temperature T1 = T0 / (1 + (γ−1)/2 · M1²) and the exit static temperature T2 = T0 / (1 + (γ−1)/2 · M2²).
Compute the inlet velocity V1 = M1 · √(γ·R·T1) and the exit velocity V2 = M2 · √(γ·R·T2) in m/s.
Report the velocity change ΔV = V2 − V1 in m/s.
The value of ΔV will be negative; state its magnitude in m/s and clearly indicate that the exit velocity is lower than the inlet velocity (i.e., a decrease, not an increase).
The only assumptions permitted are: quasi-1D flow, isentropic (no entropy generation), frictionless, and constant stagnation temperature. Do not introduce any additional assumptions.
